# Block 6: Build your own agent in R {.unnumbered} You build the two parts of an agent yourself, a conversation and a tool, then run a complete agent on a real task and approve every step it takes. After this, every control from Blocks 3 to 5 is something you can see in code. *⏱ ~45 minutes · Start on `main`, Git pane clean, with your API key saved as `AGENT_ANTHROPIC_KEY` ([setup](11a-setup-claude-code.qmd#api-key)). Claude Code is not used in this block.* :::{.callout-note collapse="true"} ## This block's files, and how it fits You stay in your workshop repository, on `main`, straight after lunch. Claude Code is set aside: you use an agent you can read line by line, and give it the translation that the shipped `tests/test_translation.R` checks. Nothing later in the day uses its output, so if time is short your instructor may run Task 2 on screen while you decide each approval in the chat. | File | Where it comes from | Its job here | |---|---|---| | `data/raw/voles_metabolism.csv` | Shipped; used since Block 2 | The data the translation summarises | | `scripts/functions/load_voles.R` | Shipped; used since Block 3 | Reads the data with fixed column types | | `agent/mini_agent.R` | Shipped; first used here | The agent: four tools, its own permission rules and Manual-mode approvals | | `tests/test_translation.R` | Shipped; first used here | Compares a tidyverse translation with the original base R code | | `scripts/functions/summaries.R` | Written by your agent, with your approval, in Task 2 | The translation | | A line in `docs/ai-log.md` | You, in Task 2 | The record | **Before you start.** ellmer, the package that talks to Claude and runs the loop, is pinned in your repository's `renv.lock`, so `renv::restore()` installed it; never run `install.packages()` inside the project. Your key comes from an Anthropic Console account, separate from a Claude subscription, and lives in your user-level `.Renviron`, outside every repository. Every request costs a little; Task 2 shows you how much the agent used. The page follows the order of Hadley Wickham's explainer [*What is an agent?*](https://substack.hadley.nz/p/what-is-an-agent): a conversation, then a tool, then the loop. Joseph Barbier's talk *50 lines of code to rebuild Claude Code in R* builds the same kind of agent; the version here is our own. ::: ## Task 1: a conversation, then a tool :::{.task} ::::{.task-header} Talk to a model, then give it a tool (8 minutes) :::: ::::{.task-container} **Goal:** see what one request to a model is, and what a tool request is, so that nothing your agent does in Task 2 is a surprise. **1. Have a conversation.** In the R console: ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} library(ellmer) key <- function() Sys.getenv("AGENT_ANTHROPIC_KEY") chat <- chat_anthropic(model = "claude-sonnet-5-5", credentials = key) chat$chat("Tell me a joke about R.") chat$chat("Explain why it is funny, in one sentence.") chat ``` ::: Printing `chat` shows the conversation as turnsOne message in a conversation with a model: either yours (the user turn) or the model’s reply (the assistant turn). Tool results go back to the model inside a user turn.. The second question works only because ellmer sends the **whole conversation so far** with each request: the model keeps nothing between requests. That is the [context window](11-AI-programming-integrated.qmd) from Block 1, and why a long conversation costs more per question. **2. Give it a tool.** A tool is an R function the model may ask you to run: ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} today <- tool( function() format(Sys.Date()), name = "today", description = "Get today's date." ) chat <- chat_anthropic(model = "claude-sonnet-5-5", credentials = key) chat$register_tool(today) chat$chat("How many days until 25 December?") chat ``` ::: The model sees only the tool's name and description. Its first reply is a request, "call `today`"; ellmer runs `today()` **on your computer** and sends the result back; then the model answers. That is two requestsOne call to the model, with the whole conversation so far, and its reply. A single question can take several requests when the model asks for tools before it answers. for one question. **You are done when** you can point, in the printed `chat`, to the tool request and to the tool result, and say which of them ran on your computer. **If it goes wrong:** if the first `chat$chat()` reports a missing or invalid key, check `Sys.getenv("AGENT_ANTHROPIC_KEY") != ""`, and restart R after editing `.Renviron`. :::: ::: ## The loop An agentAn assistant that can read across a project’s files and, depending on its permission mode, edit them and run commands, such as Claude Code. An agent acts; a chat window only advises. repeats that exchange: the harness sends the conversation, runs any tool the model asks for, adds the result, and sends it all again, until a reply asks for no tool. Every control in this course acts on one of three facts: - **The model only asks.** The harness runs each tool on your computer, so that is where Manual mode asks you, a deny rule refuses, and a hook inspects. - **Results go back to the model.** A tool that reads a data file sends that data to the provider: [Block 3's disclosure route](11d-context-disclosure-autonomy.qmd). - **The model decides when to stop.** It can loop longer than you expect, which is why a real harness has limits and a stop key. :::{.callout-tip collapse="true"} ## How it works: the loop with no model at all This code runs without an API key. It replaces the model with a pretend one that follows a script; each pass of `repeat` is one request. ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} # the tools, as plain R functions tools <- list( n_rows = function(name) { nrow(get(name, envir = as.environment("package:datasets"))) } ) # a pretend model: asks for a tool until it has two results, then answers pretend_model <- function(turns) { results <- Filter(function(t) t$role == "tool result", turns) if (length(results) == 0) { list(role = "assistant", tool = "n_rows", args = list(name = "mtcars")) } else if (length(results) == 1) { list(role = "assistant", tool = "n_rows", args = list(name = "iris")) } else { list(role = "assistant", text = paste("iris has", results[[2]]$text, "rows and mtcars has", results[[1]]$text, "so iris has more.")) } } # the harness: send the conversation, run any tool asked for, repeat question <- "Which has more rows, mtcars or iris?" turns <- list(list(role = "user", text = question)) repeat { reply <- pretend_model(turns) turns <- c(turns, list(reply)) if (is.null(reply$tool)) break # no tool asked for: this is the answer result <- do.call(tools[[reply$tool]], reply$args) turns <- c(turns, list(list(role = "tool result", text = result))) } for (t in turns) { what <- if (is.null(t$tool)) t$text else paste0("call ", t$tool, "(", t$args, ")") cat(sprintf("%-12s %s\n", t$role, what)) } ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` user Which has more rows, mtcars or iris? assistant call n_rows(mtcars) tool result 32 assistant call n_rows(iris) tool result 150 assistant iris has 150 rows and mtcars has 32 so iris has more. ``` ::: ::: `do.call()` is the only line that does anything to your computer: that is where Manual mode, deny rules and hooks act. In the real API the tool result goes back inside a user turn; ellmer does that for you. ::: ## Your agent: `agent/mini_agent.R` Your repository ships a complete agent built from the same parts, about 120 lines. Your instructor walks through it; each part matches something from this morning: - **Four tools.** `list_files()` and `read_file()` look around; `write_file()` and `run_r()` change things. - **`inside_project()` is its deny rule.** It may read inside the project, except raw data and credentials files, and write **only under `scripts/`**, so it cannot edit its checks in `tests/` or its own rules in `agent/`. - **`ask_first()` is Manual mode.** Reads go straight through; every write and every run is shown to you first, and refused unless you choose **Yes**. - **The system prompt is its instruction file.** It is not given your `AGENTS.md` (it could still open the file, like any other), and like `AGENTS.md` its prompt is only a request. `run_r()` shows the gap Block 5 found: R code can write anywhere, `data/raw/` included, and read anything you can, your `.Renviron` included. Only your approval stands in the way, which is why you read the code before you choose **Yes**; afterwards the Git pane shows any change. :::{.callout-tip collapse="true"} ## Reference: the full `agent/mini_agent.R` ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} # agent/mini_agent.R ---- # A small coding agent: Claude, four tools, and the loop ellmer runs for you. # Load it from your workshop repository with # source(here::here("agent", "mini_agent.R")) # then talk to `chat`. library(ellmer) # the model: "claude-opus-5-5" is a larger model, at a higher price per token model <- "claude-sonnet-5-5" # your API key, from the AGENT_ANTHROPIC_KEY line in your user-level .Renviron; # it has its own name so that Claude Code never offers to use it agent_key <- function() Sys.getenv("AGENT_ANTHROPIC_KEY") if (agent_key() == "") { stop("No AGENT_ANTHROPIC_KEY found: add it with usethis::edit_r_environ(), ", "then restart R.") } # the agent's own permission rules: it may read inside the project, except raw # data and credentials files, and it may write only under scripts/ ---- root <- here::here() inside_project <- function(path, write = FALSE) { full <- fs::path_norm(fs::path_abs(path, start = root)) allowed <- (full == root || fs::path_has_parent(full, root)) && !fs::path_has_parent(full, fs::path(root, "data", "raw")) && !fs::path_file(full) %in% c(".Renviron", ".env") if (write) { allowed <- allowed && fs::path_has_parent(full, fs::path(root, "scripts")) } if (!allowed) { stop("Refused: ", path, if (write) { " (the agent may write only under scripts/)" } else { " is outside the project, under data/raw/, or a credentials file" }) } full } # read tools: they observe the project and change nothing ---- list_files <- tool( # one folder at a time, at most 100 names: a recursive listing would include # every package installed in renv/, and all of it would be sent to the model function(path = ".") utils::head(list.files(inside_project(path)), 100), name = "list_files", description = "List the files and folders in one folder of the project.", arguments = list(path = type_string("A folder, relative to the project root.")), annotations = tool_annotations(read_only_hint = TRUE) ) read_file <- tool( function(path) { lines <- readLines(inside_project(path), warn = FALSE) paste(utils::head(lines, 300), collapse = "\n") # keep long files short }, name = "read_file", description = "Read a text file in the project.", arguments = list(path = type_string("A file, relative to the project root.")), annotations = tool_annotations(read_only_hint = TRUE) ) # write tools: they change the project, so they need your approval ---- write_file <- tool( function(path, content) { writeLines(content, inside_project(path, write = TRUE)) paste("Wrote", path) }, name = "write_file", description = "Replace the whole contents of a text file under scripts/.", arguments = list( path = type_string("A file under scripts/, relative to the project root."), content = type_string("The complete new contents of the file.") ) ) run_r <- tool( function(code) { out <- callr::r(function(code) utils::capture.output( tryCatch(source(exprs = parse(text = code), print.eval = TRUE), error = function(e) cat("Error:", conditionMessage(e), "\n")) ), list(code = code)) paste(utils::head(out, 60), collapse = "\n") # keep long output short }, name = "run_r", description = "Run R code in a fresh R session; return its printed output.", arguments = list(code = type_string("The R code to run.")) ) # Manual mode: show every write or run request, and ask before it happens ---- ask_first <- function(request) { if (request@name %in% c("write_file", "run_r")) { cat("\nThe agent wants to call", request@name, "with:\n") for (arg in names(request@arguments)) { cat("--", arg, "--\n", request@arguments[[arg]], "\n") } # outside an interactive session there is no one to ask, so refuse if (!interactive() || utils::menu(c("Yes", "No"), title = "Allow it?") != 1) { tool_reject() } } } chat <- chat_anthropic( model = model, credentials = agent_key, system_prompt = paste( "You are a careful R assistant working in this project.", "Read files before you change them, and check your work by running it.", "Write files only under scripts/; never edit tests/ or data/raw/.", "Code you write must work in a fresh R session, so load packages with", "library() or call them with pkg::. Say what you changed, and stop when", "the task is done." ) ) chat$register_tools(list(list_files, read_file, write_file, run_r)) chat$on_tool_request(ask_first) # how many requests the agent has sent to the model: one per assistant turn ---- count_requests <- function() { sum(vapply(chat$get_turns(), function(turn) turn@role == "assistant", logical(1))) } ``` ::: `list_files()` lists one folder and at most 100 names, and `read_file()` returns at most 300 lines: a recursive listing would include every package in `renv/`, and all of it would be sent to the model. An error in a tool does not stop the agent: ellmer sends the error message back to the model, which can try something else. `run_r()` uses a fresh R session (`callr::r()`), so it cannot change the objects in yours, and only the first 60 lines of its output go back to the model. ::: ## Task 2: run your agent :::{.task} ::::{.task-header} Run your agent (20 minutes) :::: ::::{.task-container} **Goal:** watch your own agent write, test and fix a translation while you approve every write and run, so that you see exactly where Manual mode and a deny rule act. **Start state:** `main`, Git pane clean, R's working directory at the repository's root (as it is when you open the project). **1. Load the agent.** Nothing is sent to the model yet: ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} source(here::here("agent", "mini_agent.R")) ``` ::: **2. Give it the task.** The original base R code is `legacy_rate_summary()` in `tests/test_translation.R`, which also checks the translation: ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} chat$chat(paste( "Write a function summarise_rate_tidy(data) in scripts/functions/summaries.R", "whose output matches legacy_rate_summary() in tests/test_translation.R.", "Use dplyr and the native pipe; it must work in a fresh R session.", "Write only that file, and no tests. Then run", "testthat::test_file('tests/test_translation.R') with run_r, and fix the", "function until the test passes." )) ``` ::: **3. Decide each request.** Reads run without asking. For a `write_file` or `run_r` request, read what it prints and choose **Yes** only for a write to `scripts/functions/summaries.R` or a run of the test. **Refuse the first test run on purpose:** the agent stops and explains. Then let it continue: ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} chat$chat("Go ahead and run the test.") ``` ::: **4. Look inside.** ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} chat # every turn: your prompt, its tool requests, the results count_requests() # how many requests it sent to the model chat$get_tokens() # the tokens it sent and received ``` ::: **5. Check its work yourself.** The agent's "the test passes" is a claim. Read the diff of `scripts/functions/summaries.R` in the Git pane, then restart R (*Session → Restart R*) and run: ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} testthat::test_dir(here::here("tests")) ``` ::: **6. Record and commit.** Add a line to `docs/ai-log.md` with today's date, for example `2026-10-22; mini agent (ellmer, claude-sonnet-5-5); translated the rate summary to tidyverse; kept after reading the diff and running the tests`, then commit `summaries.R` and the log.
`aggregate()` with a formula silently drops the animal whose `metabolic_rate_post` is missing, so the original's mean and count leave it out. A literal tidyverse translation keeps it: an `NA` mean and a count one too high. The test compares against the original, so the agent had to match that behaviour, and if it read the test it probably did so without comment. The test checks "the same as the original", not "correct": Block 8 returns to that difference.
**You are done when** `test_translation.R` passes in your own run, the Git pane showed only `summaries.R` and your log changed, you can say how many requests and tokens the task took, and both are committed. **If it goes wrong:** - **The agent loops or goes off course:** answer **No**, then steer it with `chat$chat("…")`, or `source()` the file again to start a new conversation. - **A refused path you expected to work:** check `getwd()` is the repository's root. - **An unwanted change:** **Revert** it in the Git pane. :::{.callout-tip collapse="true"} ## What did it cost? `chat$get_cost()` turns the tokens into money when ellmer knows the model's price. If it shows `NA`, run `ellmer::models_update_prices()` once to refresh ellmer's price list, or multiply the tokens from `chat$get_tokens()` by the prices on Anthropic's pricing page. `claude-opus-5-5`, set at the top of `mini_agent.R`, is a larger model at a higher price per token. ::: :::: ::: ## What Claude Code adds | Your mini agent | Claude Code | |---|---| | `ask_first()` and `tool_reject()` | Manual mode (`default`) and the other permission modes | | `inside_project()`: writes only under `scripts/` | Deny rules in `.claude/settings.json`, such as `Edit(/data/raw/**)` | | The system prompt | `AGENTS.md`, read at the start of each session | | `run_r()` in a fresh R session | Commands it runs in the Terminal; you check results in a fresh R session | | `chat`, `count_requests()`, `chat$get_tokens()` | The conversation itself, and the model shown in Claude Code | | Git | Git | Claude Code adds plan mode, hooks, skills, compaction of long conversations, many more tools and far more checks around each one. Building the small version is a way to understand the big one, not a reason to use it for real work. In Block 7 you hand Claude Code a much bigger job under the same controls. :::{.callout-note} ## Check · Reproduce · Record - **You can now:** explain an agent as a model, a harness and tools in a loop, and run one in R, **trusted because** you can read every line that touches your files, and a test you did not write decides whether its change is right. - **Check:** every write and every run is shown to you before it happens; the Git pane shows what changed; the test runs in a fresh R session. - **Reproduce:** `run_r()` runs in a fresh R session, so the agent's checks do not depend on what is loaded in yours. - **Record:** `chat` holds the full record of what was sent and received; your AI-use log records the tool, the model and what you kept. ::: ## Check your understanding **In an agent built with ellmer, who runs a tool's R function?**
**True or false: when an agent's tool reads a file, the file's contents are sent to the model provider.** **`inside_project()` lets the agent write only under `scripts/`. Which tool call could still change a raw data file?**
## Going further (not covered live) This material is not covered in the live session. Work through it afterwards if it is useful to you. :::{.callout-tip collapse="true"} ## Add a `run_tests` tool Replace general-purpose `run_r()` for checking with a tool that can only run the project's tests, `function() testthat::test_dir("tests")` run through `callr::r()`. A narrow tool needs less approval than a general one: you might let it through without asking, and keep asking for `run_r()`. ::: :::{.callout-tip collapse="true"} ## A restricted mode Change `ask_first()` so it asks before every call, reads included. You then see every file the agent wants to read before it is sent to the provider, which is the habit Block 3 recommends near confidential data. ::: :::{.callout-tip collapse="true"} ## Packages that do more - [btw](https://posit-dev.github.io/btw/) gives ellmer agents ready-made tools for R: package documentation, your live session's objects and your project's files. - [mcptools](https://posit-dev.github.io/mcptools/) connects R to the Model Context Protocol, so R functions can be tools for other assistants, including Claude Code. ::: :::{.callout-tip collapse="true"} ## Another provider ellmer has a `chat_*()` function for each provider it supports, and the tools and loop stay the same. Tool calling can be much less reliable with small local models, so start with a hosted model. ::: ## Glossary ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ::: {.cell-output-display} `````{=html}
term definition
agent An assistant that can read across a project's files and, depending on its permission mode, edit them and run commands, such as Claude Code. An agent acts; a chat window only advises.
request One call to the model, with the whole conversation so far, and its reply. A single question can take several requests when the model asks for tools before it answers.
turn One message in a conversation with a model: either yours (the user turn) or the model's reply (the assistant turn). Tool results go back to the model inside a user turn.
````` ::: ::: ## References - Wickham, H. (2026, 5 June). *What is an agent?* AI for data science (Substack). - Barbier, J. *50 lines of code to rebuild Claude Code in R*. Talk abstract, 10 November (year and venue not stated in the abstract). - Wickham, H., Cheng, J., Jacobs, A., Aden-Buie, G. and Schloerke, B. (2026). *ellmer: Chat with large language models*.
